snippet.title: David Fincher on CLIFF BOOTH, MINDHUNTER, ALIEN 3, ZODIAC, his BATMAN & STAR WARS pitches, & more!
snippet.description:
David Fincher, HSC’s most anticipated guest, finally joins the podcast. Fincher sits down with Josh for Happy Sad Confused’s longest episode yet: an hour-and-a-half deep dive into one of the greatest living directors’ filmography, from ALIEN 3’s original pitch, to the opening sequence of SEVEN, to what drew him to collaborating with Quentin Tarantino on his latest film, THE FURTHER MIS-ADVENTURES OF CLIFF BOOTH. Find out why he won’t make another season of MINDHUNTER, how he shot the most disturbing scene in ZODIAC, and why he sees actors better than anyone. Plus, Fincher shares what his pitches were for STAR WARS, BATMAN, SPIDER-MAN, & more! This is an extensive, career-spanning conversation for any Fincher fan out there. Enjoy!

snippet.title: Sacha Baron Cohen on ALI G: WHO IZ I?, BORAT, Quentin Tarantino, Mephisto, & more!
snippet.description:
The incomparable Sacha Baron Cohen joins HSC in honor of his new film, ALI G: WHO IZ I? Not only is Sacha a one-of-a-kind actor, he’s also an amazing storyteller. From sharing the surprising reason why he chose to bring back Ali G now, to giving a peek into his joke editing process, to recounting the lengths he went to in order to nail the shocking scenes in the film–if you’ve loved ALI G, BORAT, BRUNO, or any of Sacha’s characters, this is an in-depth conversation about the method behind the madness. Plus, tips on how to deliver the most Borat-esque “my wife,” the moment that made him feel seen by the MCU team, how he’s prepping to star in Quentin Tarantino’s latest project, and more!

Recorded at the 92nd Street Y

snippet.title: Michael Douglas on ONE HELLUVA RIDE, WALL STREET, ANT-MAN, BEHIND THE CANDELABRA, & more!
snippet.description:
The one and only Michael Douglas joins the podcast. Michael bares all in his new memoir, ONE HELLUVA RIDE, and he sits down with Josh to share an even more in-depth look at the book’s revelations–plus a few that didn’t make it to the page. From telling his father, Kirk Douglas, that he wanted to act, to getting pushed by Oliver Stone on the set of WALL STREET, to an account of what it was like to film intimate scenes before an intimacy coordinator became the standard, to why he decided to do ANT-MAN, this episode is a treat for anyone who’s resonated with Michael’s prolific life. 
Recorded at the 92nd Street Y
